stages.title: Points and position vectors
body: A point in 3D has three coordinates: how far along the x-, y- and z-axes it is. The point A is {{pt:L1.a}}.
The position vector of A goes from the origin O to A. We call it {{v:a}} and write it as a column vector: {{v:a}} = {{col:L1.a}}.
Each entry is the distance to move parallel to one axis, in the order x, y, z.

stages.title: The vector equation of a line
body: A line is fixed by one point on it and a direction. Here the point is A, with position vector {{v:a}}, and the direction vector is {{v:b}} = {{col:L1.b}}.
Every point on the line has a position vector {{v:r}} of the form {{v:r}} = {{v:a}} + λ{{v:b}}. For this line, {{eq:L1}}.
The parameter λ picks the point. λ = 0 gives A itself, and each extra 1 added to λ moves one step of {{v:b}} along the line. Negative values go the other way.
Drag the λ slider and watch the point and its coordinates.
notes: {{v:b}} sets the direction. Any non-zero multiple of {{v:b}} describes the same direction.

stages.title: Parallel lines
body: Its direction vector is a multiple of the direction of L₁: {{multiple:L3,L1}}. So L₁ and L₃ point the same way. They are parallel.
Parallel lines could still be the same line, so test one point. {{notOn:L3,L1}} So L₁ and L₃ are parallel and distinct: they never meet.
notes: Two lines are parallel when their direction vectors are multiples of each other.

stages.title: Intersecting lines
body: Their directions are not multiples of each other, so they are not parallel. If the lines meet, some value of λ and some value of μ give the same point. Set the two position vectors equal:
So the lines meet at {{meet:L1,L2}}, where λ = {{p1:L1,L2}} and μ = {{p2:L1,L2}}. Set both sliders to these values and the two points coincide.
notes: Solve two of the equations, then always check the third. The check decides whether the lines really meet.

stages.title: Skew lines
body: Compare it with L₁. Are the lines parallel? Do they meet?

interaction.heading: Predict, then reveal
interaction.question: From this view, L₁ and L₄ seem to cross. Do they actually meet?
interaction.prompt: Make your prediction first. Then reveal the answer and watch the view turn.
reveal: No, they never meet. The directions {{col:L1.b}} and {{col:L4.b}} are not multiples of each other, so the lines are not parallel either.
The three equations have no common solution, so there is no point on both lines. Lines that are not parallel and do not meet are called skew.
Skew lines can only happen in 3D. In a flat plane, two lines that are not parallel always meet. From one particular view they can look as if they cross, but turning the view shows the gap.
interaction.revealNote: Going further: the shortest distance between L₁ and L₄ is {{dist:L1,L4}}. The closest points are {{closest:L1,L4}}. The segment PQ is parallel to {{pq:L1,L4}}, which is perpendicular to both lines.

controls.speedHint: Changes how fast the point moves along the line.
controls.hint: Drag to orbit. Scroll or pinch to zoom. Moving a slider pauses the animation.
